Hike Crew Advanced Portable Outdoor Camping and Travel Toilet – Adult Porta Potty w/Level Indicator, Rotating Spout, Pressure Valve, 3-Way Pistol Flush – for RV, Boat or Trailer – 5.3 Gallon (20L) The thing is well built and should work perfectly. It's well designed. It really should work.

Mine has a manufacturing flaw where the handle on the valve to the lower tank does not completely clear the plastic of the unit when closing. It sits right up against the edge of the plastic, and if you move the thing around too much, or if it changes temperature substantially (e.g. in the trunk of a vehicle) then the handle gets pushed out a tiny bit. That opens the lower tank *just enough* that gasses seep out. I had it in my shed for a few days and came back and the whole shed reeked of that tank.

I will still use the thing but not in an enclosed building or similar. In a standup tent it should be fine. Maybe mine is just an outlier in material thickness or something.

text_fidelity_a:
Palio Master 2.0 Table Tennis Racket & Case - ITTF Approved - Flared - Intermediate Ping Pong, Racket, Paddle There are a lot of terrible premade rackets. I've used several different rackets from Stiga and Joola and they were all really bad. The thing that really sets the Palio rackets apart is the high quality CJ8000 rubber. The grip and durability is just so much better than what you would normally get from a premade racket. I would also like to point out that the rubber lasts a LOT longer than the cheap garbage that they normally put on premade rackets. I've been using this paddle for about 35-40 hours of game play and there is almost no loss in grip.

Overall the racket has a nice crisp response and pretty good speed. It's a little bit faster than the average racket and has good control. The feedback (feel) from the blade is good and I haven't noticed any dead spots when striking the ball.

The interesting thing about this racket is that the rubbers are designed to peel off easily so that they can be replaced. (Almost all premade rackets have non-removable rubber) A lot of Amazon customers seem to be complaining about the rubbers coming loose. ITS SUPPOSED TO PEEL OFF EASILY! If it's a little loose on the edge just glue it. I plan to eventually peel off the forehand rubber and replace it with something more aggressive when I get better at looping.

The only complaint I have is that the wood finish on the handle is a little rough. Some people like that, but I prefer a smoother grip.
text_fidelity_b: Palio Master 2.0 Table Tennis Racket & Case - ITTF Approved - Flared - Intermediate Ping Pong, Racket, Paddle

text_fidelity_a:
Swingbyte 2 Golf Training Device - Golf’s Most Trusted Mobile Swing Analyzer - Includes Mobile App for iPhone and Android The app that accompanies this and the way it works is simple and very neat. I have yet to have a chance to check it vs more expensive industry standards like GC2 or trackman BUT for the most part these devices are accurate unto themselves and it's user error that throws them off.

It does NOT do carry distance (which makes sense if you think about it, it doesn't see what the ball is doing). If you duff a shot fat and hit the deck before the ball, it will register that as your strike.

It has a very cool animation and 3D manipulated graphic and pretty much all the important info in terms of face angle/path/AoA/speed/shaft lean. All very good for the home golf nerd that doesn't have regular access to the big machines.

Where it falls short and loses a star from my perspective is this: The mounting system needs a good bit of work. I left it in my car on a hot day inside the little carrying case it comes in (it latches to a little plastic dowel) and when doing so I THINK it melted the rubber grippers that grab onto the club shaft. So now it doesn't have enough tension to hold onto smooth steel shafts (like on irons). So after a few solid strikes taking divots or some poorly struck shots that rattle the club you will notice that the device is no longer in line with your club face. Who knows how long it's been that way so unless you check every time your data for the day could be total garbage. Another thing, the cover that protects the USB charging port is ALSO the aligning mark. This presents two problems. 1 the darn thing keeps opening and flopping around while I try to swing. 2 This alignment mark which is suppose to assist in the ultimate accuracy of the device is on a component that is NOT securely fashioned onto the device itself.

Bottom line: Quite a fun and when used carefully possibly quite accurate tool to help you make your swing easier to quantify and tangible. Not perfect but maybe there will be a Swingbyte 3 that will address these things :)
text_fidelity_b: Swingbyte 2 Golf Training Device - Golf’s Most Trusted Mobile Swing Analyzer - Includes Mobile App for iPhone and Android

Super Bright Bike Light USB Rechargeable, Te-Rich 1200 Lumens Waterproof Road/Mountain Bicycle Headlight and LED Taillight Set with 4400 mAh Battery I previously purchased a BLITZU Gator 390 light for my bike and it was OK but not as bright as I wanted. When the mount for the BLITZU light broke, after a few months, I was unable to get any response from the manufacturer so I gave up and bought this light to replace it.

This light is head and shoulders above the BLITZU light. The new light is incredibly bright. I find myself using it on its lowest intensity setting and have more than enough light to deal with beach front bike paths here in southern California. I would hesitate to use the brighter settings because I think it might blind other cyclists who are coming toward me. I can see using the brighter settings in strobe mode during the day if I am riding in places with automobile traffic.

The power pack is very much like a standard USB power pack like the ones used to charge smart phones. So I can carry a spare battery on the outside chance that the standard battery dies. My previous light had a built in battery and if it died I would have been out of luck.

The mount seems more substantial than the one on the BLITZU light but it is plastic so I assume it will degrade from sun exposure sooner or later. Fortunately the light attaches to the mount with a standard camera tripod type thread so there are lots of alternative mounts available on Amazon and elsewhere.

The light seems to be very well made of machined aluminum.

The only issue I have with the design is that it is necessary to thread the light onto the screw that comes out of the mount so you have to spin the light 360 degrees several times to attach it. This can be a problem if you have other things mounted near the bike light mount on your handlebars as adjacent devices can prevent the light from rotating.
I had to mount it farther off center than I wanted so it was clear of my cell phone mount.. I would like it better if the stud that the light mounts on could be rotated up into the light using a thumb screw.

The tail light that came with it looks to be decently made and is bright enough. The tail light runs off two flat mercury cells. There are no instructions for the tail light so it took me a few minutes to figure out that there was a thin sheet of plastic between the two batteries in the light that had to be removed before the light would would work.

The instructions for the headlight were minimal. There was no information about how to charge the battery and how many hours of light would be provided, for the various power levels, before the battery would fail. All the instructions you would need would probably fit on one side of a 3x5 index card and that would be a nice addition to the product.

The light came with a headband mount so you can use this light as a head mounted light. Im not a big fan of those lights because I find myself frequently shining the light directly in the face of people I speak with and that, of course, ruins their night vision for a few minutes.

It would be nice if there was some way to control the size of the beam for the headlight. Most of the time I would like it to be a little wider than it is. But I can live with the current design if making the beam width adjustable would impact the waterproof design of this light.
text_fidelity_b: Super Bright Bike Light USB Rechargeable, Te-Rich 1200 Lumens Waterproof Road/Mountain Bicycle Headlight and LED Taillight Set with 4400 mAh Battery

text_fidelity_a:
Bushnell 14MP Trophy Cam HD Aggressor Low Glow Trail Camera, Brown I was looking forward to having found a good camera here, but disappointed. Similar to a sister company's Primos 02 camera that I tried, I found that the field of the motion sensor was misaligned with the field of the picture. I determined this by walking past the camera to observe the results. Consequently, animals to the right of the picture field of view would set it off and you might not get them in a picture at all. And animals walking from left to right would not trigger it until well past center of the picture. The Primos 02 misalignment was worse but the Bushnell wasn't good.

On the positive, the pictures and videos from this camera were very good; superior to the Primos 02 and another camera I tried. The wide screen picture was perfect for my use. The settings allow for both shutter speed and LED intensity which certainly should be useful to adjust for how far away your primary target area is. It is because of the picture quality that I thought I had found the right camera for me. The Hybrid feature to take both pictures followed by videos is great. Unlike the Primos 02, I didn't have excessive false positive pictures.

But then, I changed the shutter speed and LED settings to take pictures on a closer target area which resulted in the camera taking pictures and videos constantly, nearly 1000 in a 24 hour period. If the "Field Scan" were set to ON, that might have been the result but I had it set to OFF. Of course, two days of this drained the batteries.

Another difficulty is that when set to take three burst pictures, the delay was too quick. Per the time stamp, all three would snap within a single second and you cannot adjust this. So your animal hardly had any time to move further through the field of view.

The camera came with current firmware, so an older version firmware was not to blame for these issues. Possibly the product was defective but I returned it for refund rather than exchange, largely because with my Primos 02 experience an exchange of cameras did not fix the misalignment.
text_fidelity_b: Bushnell 14MP Trophy Cam HD Aggressor Low Glow Trail Camera, Brown

text_fidelity_a:
Black Diamond Spot Headlamp My favorite low priced headlamp.
Not the quality of high tech wonder lamps. But there are no real faults. And the interface is very good.
All inputs on one button which is the best way to do it, fewer moving parts to go wrong.
3 inputs : momentary push, 3 second push, 6 second push.
If the lamp is on :
Momentary push cycles on/off.
Long push gradually dims the light in steps.
(when it reaches the dimmest it will flicker once to indicate lowest level,
then it gradually brightens the light, step at a time, flickers once on highest).
This works very well to set the brightness levels.

When light is OFF:
momentary push turns it on (two outer lights for flood, or center for spot. Repeat pushes will alternate: spot, off, flood, off, spot,...
3 second push : turns on the red lamp
6 second push: turns on the lock mode (locks lamp off until another 6 sec. push turns it back on. A blue light on the side will go on for a couple seconds to verify the lamp is locked).

I find the interface easy to use to get it to do as I like when I like.
5 different tilt settings from straight down to higher than straight forward. There are settings I find perfect for reading or watching your step on the trail. And they stay put.

Very bright on spot!
The flood is very spread out, lights up the whole room or tent.

5 stars.
------

Another lamp that costs about $10 more is the Princeton Tec EOS TACTICAL. The tactical model of the EOS line is military issue from several governments. Bulletproof and rugged, really waterproof. But the ergonomics are military rough: the button is very hard to push (so it won't wear out), the battery box takes a tool like a dime to open (so they could never fall out by mistake). A better choice if you going to climb mount Everest and your life depends on the lamp. Not as good as this BDSH for using in common outdoor camping, running, hunting, imo.

Those are the two under $50 that I like.

EDIT: I should have noted the reviews stating the tilt lock stops would fail. They failed in 6 months on one of mine of these. The other two I have are getting weaker and weaker (about a year old). Then the lamp just tilts all the way forward and points at your toes. No way to reset the tilt after the mechanism breaks. I changed my rating from 5 stars to 2 stars. I do NOT recommend these.
text_fidelity_b: Black Diamond Spot Headlamp

I can't always say the same for the rods or reels, but the line rarely ever snaps. I love that it is such a low profile line too. Like the diameter of the line is far thinner than the comparable monofilament version, and MUCH easier to tie than the thick plastic stuff. I find the plastic monofilament stuff is harder to get the knot to hold than the braided lines. Yes it is certainly far more expensive than the monofilament ones, but in my personal opinion, it is worth every penny to pay that little extra and rarely ever have to worry about losing that lunker because your line snapped. I have seen the hooks BEND before this line snaps, which to me is pretty darned impressive.

CamelBak Eddy+ Water Bottle with Straw 20 oz - Insulated Stainless Steel I am INCREDIBLY disappointed because I ordered this for hot liquids because the Amazon description says "double-wall vacuum insulated to maintain cold or hot temperatures." However, once I received this and saw the plastic / rubberized tip and a similar type straw, I thought there is no way this is for hot liquid. I was right. After reading the attached card (see first photo), it says this is not for hot liquid. I have so many cold liquid containers that I did not want another one. This is also expensive and is not worth the purchase for just a cold beverage container when it was a hot liquid container that was wanted.

Nevertheless, it works very well for cold liquids very well. This comes in three pieces (reservoir, top, straw). The straw gets screwed into the top. The tip is pliable and has to be sipped with strong suction. My water stayed cold all night long. I did put several ice cubes in the container with my tepid water and it felt like it came out of the fridge after about 12 hours.

In addition to its thermal properties, it is also leakproof.

In summary, this is four stars as a cold beverage insulating container but zero stars for hot simply because the straw and tip are not suitable for that. Had this "hot liquid" incorrect claim not been made on the Amazon site (which is how all purchasers make decisions), I would have rated this 4 stars.
text_fidelity_b: CamelBak Eddy+ Water Bottle with Straw 20 oz - Insulated Stainless Steel

text_fidelity_a:
Cathe Friedrich's Supersets & Push Pull DVD (Body Blast series) On this DVD, master instructor Cathe Friedrich offers two workouts from her Body Blast series: Supersets, a strength workout in which exercises are performed in rounds, and Push Pull, a strength workout focused on opposing muscle groups. Both workouts are very good, but what really makes this DVD so valuable is the wide variety of customization options as described below.

Supersets is a 53 minute workout. In each round, Cathe does separate exercises to work the legs, back, chest, shoulders/biceps/triceps, and core. After a brief (4-minute) warm-up, there are a total of two rounds, each broken down into two series (A and B). Cathe encourages participants to lift as heavy as possible, and she incorporates use of a barbell, dumbbells, a stability ball, and unweighted exercises as well. Many exercises are non-traditional in nature, as they include "low end" pluses as well as plyometric moves such as jump squats. The workout makes nice use of the stability ball, particularly for the core work, and Cathe finishes with 5.5 minutes of floor stretches.

Push Pull is a 45-minute, full-body weight training routine which works opposing muscle groups. In some cases, the muscle group is worked with only one exercise, whereas other muscles are targeted with several different exercises. Equipment used for this workout includes a tall step, a stability ball, a barbell, and several sets of dumbbells. The workout begins with a 3-minute warm-up which consists of some light cardio plus stretches using the tall step. Cathe then jumps right in on the legs, performing squats with the barbell, deadlifts, lunges (placing one heel on a smaller barbell to increase the work to the quads), and tall box presses. Moving on to the upper body, Cathe does chest press and rows, then ball work, includnig chest flyes and a "Y" move. Additional upper body work includes a shoulder press off the step, a one-arm row, a front raise while seated on the ball, a rear delt raise lying on the ball, bicep work with one leg on the ball for balance, and tricep dips/kickbacks. Cathe also incorporates the ball for floor leg work such as outer thigh lifts and inner thigh squeezes. There is also additional back work, abs work, and calf raises. Cathe concludes with a short (4.5 minutes) stretch that includes some nice shoulder stretches.

As mentioned above, the best thing about this DVD is the wide variety of custom options. The menus for both Supersets and Push Pull include options for playing the entire workout, viewing the chapter selections, and mixing and matching chapters. In addition, each workout offers "Quick Select Premixes" which provide both shorter and longer workout options. For Supersets, there are 14 premixes ranging in length from 28-109 minutes (these include extra cycles, upper/lower body only, etc.), and for Push Pull, there are 7 premixes ranging from 18-77 minutes which also included upper/lower body only options. Finally, there is a "Workout Blender" option which allows you to create your own custom workout by selecting chapters from either Supersets or Push Pull.

If you are familiar with Cathe, you know that she often incorporates upbeat, recognizable music (selections here include "Goldeneye," "Unbreak My Heart," "Walking in Memphis," and "Breakfast at Tiffany's"). Both workouts are solid, intermediate-level routines which will definitely help you to target virtually every body part from head-to-toe; my overall rating is 4 1/2 starts, and I would definitely recommend this DVD to others.
text_fidelity_b: Cathe Friedrich's Supersets & Push Pull DVD (Body Blast series)

text_fidelity_a:
The Firm Zip Trainer Medicine Ball Kit I chose this workout system a bit blindly, but I'm glad I picked it to try out. Having recently been diagnosed as type-2 diabetic, I've been working on managing my condition by adding some daily physical activity and changing my eating habits. Just with walking 30 minutes a day has resulted in my losing about 20 pounds in the past three months (I want to lose 20 more). Now that I've lost weight, I find that I need to tone up. Being over 50, I wanted to do something that was easy to do and low-impact. This Firm Zip Trainer system is perfect for that.

Watching the videos for the first time I really didn't think this was much of a workout - but found trying the exercise that wasn't true. The series of movements that the instructors put you through really work and stretch your muscles. I think that is the thing I like most about these exercises, you get to use muscles that you probably don't use on a daily basis (especially if you're like me someone who sits at a computer for most of the day). I really feel my range of motion has improved since starting this program.

I've only been using this for about a month, and not every day at that. You need some room to do these exercise, and right now the largest clear space I can come up with is my unheated garage. And given it's winter, there's been a number of days when it was too cold to exercise out there.

With this kit, you get the large medicine ball - which can be zipped open to be used in a variety of ways. The medicine ball by itself is five pounds and when put the three pound core ball in it, it becomes eight pounds. That doesn't seem like a lot of weight, but when you're out of shape as I am you will get tired after just a couple repetitions. You also get three DVDs, two of which are the main exercise programs and a third which is a bonus video. You start with disc one, which walks you through the basics of the routines. There are four programs on disc one. Rev!, which is sort of introduction and runs for about 15 minutes, and three full length workouts (22 minutes each) - one for cardio, one to sculpt, and one that is and amped up routine. Each of the programs usually features three of the six instructors, with one leading the exercise and the other two in the background with one doing a modified starter version of the routine and the other doing a more advanced version. The instructor will explain the routine and do a quick demonstration before starting. It can be hard to follow along - so I would recommend watching the videos without doing them first, then go back and follow along. Also of note, the Zip ball doesn't get used in all the exercises - there are even some where they use regular weights (looks like they are using 10 pound dumbbells). They also use typical exercise mat for some things.

The exercise sets on the second DVDs are more of the same, but gives you more of a workout. The bonus DVD is a routine that works your feet (you do it bare foot) and your abs.

My guess is most people will watch the videos a couple times and then once they learn the routines quit playing them. I also think that people will cherry pick certain parts of the routines and create their own versions of the workouts (least that I what I will be doing). Like I mentioned before, I'm a bit over fifty and out of shape, so there is a limit to what I can do right now - as I improve I'll add in more.

Something to note - there are a couple booklets that come with this set. One of which has bios of the six trainers that are featured on the videos. These are some really fit women, and I assumed most of them were a lot younger that they apparently are. The youngest is 31 (or was when these were made), and the oldest is 43 (and most of them have had children). That really surprised me.

The other booklet that you get is a 48-page nutrition guide / meal planner. I mentioned I had already been losing weight and I've done that by going to a high-protein/low-carbohydrate diet (which is what my doctor recommended for my diabetes). This nutrition guide recommends that too. The booklet really doesn't provide any detailed recipes, but it does give you a pretty decent meal plan to follow (very similar to the one I was provided by my diabetes educator).

To wrap up this review I'll say that I'm enjoying this Zip Trainer kit, and I liked it enough that I went and bought the [[ASIN:B0056H4GHK The Firm Express DVD Kit]].

Something to maybe mention that might interest some people, these videos are a product of GAIAM, which is the company that also puts out most of the DVD sets for the Discovery Channel - shows like Mythbusters and Dirty Jobs.
text_fidelity_b: The Firm Zip Trainer Medicine Ball Kit

text_fidelity_a:
Raqpak Beach/Picnic Blanket, Lightweight and Sand Proof with 4 Stakes, 7 x 7 Feet The picnic blanket that we have used for years is a classic red and white checker pattern vinyl rectangle. It's fine for small outings and it does provide a moisture barrier but it is small and not suitable for more than just one or two people. This is a very different blanket, suitable for picnics and for the beach and much better suited for larger groups.

Unlike a terrycloth blanket or a vinyl sheet, this blanket is made of parachute nylon which has the advantages of being very lightweight and water resistant. It also is very non-bulky and folds up into a small and compact bundle in the *attached* bag, to a size that is slightly smaller than the average purse. I would not have thought it would pack this small, but it's absolutely perfect for packing for a trip.

When completely unfolded this blanket is 7'x7', more than adequate for a group of 4-6 people. Being as light as it is, without anchoring at the corners it can easily get caught in the wind and blow around. So, each corner has a small elastic loop and included with the blanket is a set of 4 small stakes so that it can be better anchored down. Additionally, there are pockets on the corners so that additional weight can be added (rocks or sand) which helps even more when the ground is not suitable for relying solely on stakes. The packing bag doubles as a stash bag for things like sunglasses or a phone or it can be used to hold trash items until it's time to pack up again.

Though this is marketed predominantly a blanket it is more useful to me and to my family as a table cloth for picnic tables. Skyline Drive in Shenandoah National Park has several picnic areas that are wonderful places to stop and spend time for lunch and this blanket covers those picnic tables nicely. The packing bag again serves double duty - it works well for holding utensils (spoons, ladles, etc.) while the blanket is spread on the table and it can again hold small amounts of trash until packing up to leave.

This blanket is a very simple but very nice product that serves multiple purposes. It's fine for use on the beach and it works just for as a picnic blanket but it's just as useful as a picnic table cover. It packs up very nicely and is extremely portable and is not unreasonably priced.

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: Raqpak Beach/Picnic Blanket, Lightweight and Sand Proof with 4 Stakes, 7 x 7 Feet

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Basics Strap-On Wedge Saddle Bag for Cycling The saddle bag is a decent, basic product that suits its purpose. Here are some specific points:
Size: You have the dimensions, so you know the size. It’s tapered from top to bottom, so that’s something to consider beyond just the dimensions. It’s not a commuter bag—not its intent—and so its size is more than suitable I’d say for those little things you might want to carry with you on a ride: you phone, keys, whatever you carry money in (for those who still carry money). You can fit a tube and tool set in for peace of mind, but that will obviously reduce room for those other things depending on their size.

Form: as mentioned, it’s tapered toward the bottom so it fits against the bike under the seat. It’s pretty long, so you’ll want to make sure it will fit under the seat—I can see some bikes not having space for it depending on how high their seat is raised (mine is just on the edge of this being a good fit). Same is true if you have a rack over your back wheel (for panniers)—it’s so long that there’s a decent chance it will overlap the rear part of the rack. It is flexible enough to crunch down and reduce its footprint, but obviously then you’ve ust lost some of its total space.

There’s a small mesh pocket inside to keep something separate (in other words so it doesn’t just mix in the large space, making it easier for instance to grab your keys instead of fishing around). It’s a decent solution but I would have preferred if it had also zipped.

Construction: it seems solidly built enough. The material appears pretty tough, as if it will handle wear and tear well, along with the elements. I’m not sure about how it will do with rain (at least not yet). I don’t get a sense (and there was no documentation) that it is water “proof”, but my guess would be it is at least somewhat water “resistant” based on the feel and construction of the material. Personally, until you’ve experienced a good rainfall (we’re in drought conditions here) and can see how it deals, I’d put anything valuable in a plastic bag.

Mounting: Simple and easy. Three straps/loops that give it good stability. Thanks to the three straps and the size, it doesn’t move/shift around at all under my seat.

So a nice little carry-on but definitely check that the length will work for you (especially people with their seat pretty low).
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics Strap-On Wedge Saddle Bag for Cycling

text_fidelity_a:
Topeak Mondo Pack with Fixer F25 with Extendable Back Pocket, 12.6 x 5.1 x 6.3-Inch (X-Large) A great product, certainly up to Topeak's standards. The pouch is huge and very roomy. It has a great side compartment to prevent your tools from beating up your snacks, and has a nice mesh pocket perfect for CO2 cartridges. Two caveats are worth considering. First, there is a temptation to stuff the main compartment full of stuff, and this is a great idea for a long ride. If you do so, it will require some unpacking to get to all of the gear, so pack the stuff you want to access quickly (e.g. food!) near the zipper. You can pack the tubes out of the way, if you blow one, you likely don't have a problem with the extra minute it takes you to get to it. The second issue to be aware of is that this pack is HUGE. Measure your bike to make sure that it fits, and make sure that you are happy with the look (it looks nothing like a wedge pack).

I was aware of both issues, and I love the pack! It lets me ride VERY long rides on my road bike without support and without a trunk bag.
text_fidelity_b: Topeak Mondo Pack with Fixer F25 with Extendable Back Pocket, 12.6 x 5.1 x 6.3-Inch (X-Large)

The biggest problem is that the video quality is awful. I play a lot of old games from the Fairchild Channel F to the Sega Genesis and this looks worse than any of my dozen consoles. It's not because I'm playing it on a modern TV that upscales it badly - I play this on my HDTV with a RetroTink that makes the NES look like a million bux. It's just that the video output from this thing is really sorry. Play it on a CRT if you still have one - that will soften the flaws a little bit.

I'm very sad that the plug'n'play generation ended here because a version of this with HDMI out and Wii-style accelerometers to more accurately detect nudges would make for an amazing experience. I'm still giving this five stars because the tables are great and it feels great to play, and it costs as much as a frugal fast casual lunch. If you can never get enough pinball, don't miss out on this thing.

text_fidelity_a:
Simmons 20-60X60 Venture Black Fmcwptripodhard/Soft Case This old bird still has some of the original low power hunting scopes made by Simmons back in the day. I always wondered why my Dad had a 4X Leupold scope on his .22 while I had a Simmons 4X. Although the Simmons did an acceptable job, it was in no way comparable to the Leupold. Of course my Dad's .22 rimfire rifle was also far superior to the Sears model that he bought for me. But believe me, I was just thrilled at age 10 to be able to go squirrel hunting. And since I trained all winter at the local armory, I could hold my own against him.

But enough of the old days. Simmons then was considered a fairly mediocre manufacturer. Now Simmons is a brand owned by Bushnell Corporation (acquired by them in 2008) which in turn is owned by Vista Outdoor. Competition in the optics market and great strides made in this technology has resulted in current offerings superior in quality and also very reasonably priced. That is an example of "value engineering" at its finest.

This Simmons spotting scope was shipped in a hard case and had the scope itself also wrapped in plastic and inside a separate soft case. Well protected indeed! A bench sized tripod is also included as are directions for both locating the instruction manual and for registering the product for potential warranty coverage. Fear not for the instruction sheet is offered in five languages.

Being an older guy and not a hunter, I don't have to worry about lugging this rather large scope through the bushes. However it does serve two needs for me. The first is that it is extremely useful when testing .22 ammo at a 100 yard range. These old eyes are not what they used to be and this Simmons scope makes it simple to track and score my shots. Most of my shooting is suppressed and testing various subsonic ammo has been interesting to say the least.

Since we live on beautiful Charlotte Harbor in Southwest Florida, Mother Nature offers us constant reminders of how the animal kingdom functions and survives. Being able to focus on long distances off our back lanai has really increased our visual reach even to the far shore. We are able to watch Bald Eagles and Osprey fish, Red Tailed Hawks and Florida Barred Owls home in on their prey, and alligators and manatees cruise through the harbor. Entertaining for us and our guests.

For roughly $150.00 this is a heck of a deal for the quality you receive. Simmons has worked its way back into being competitive with most of the mainstream firms. If you're looking for a big increase in quality, plan on spending a lot more money. In the old days we would call this "the law of diminishing returns". That means that you have to spend a lot more money just to get an incremental return in actual performance. Simmons proves that you don't have to spend that much.
text_fidelity_b: Simmons 20-60X60 Venture Black Fmcwptripodhard/Soft Case

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in)) My first one wouldn't hold a charge for longer than a day and a half, but I was able to rather easily get a refund for that one, and purchase a brand new one.

I use the iPhone app almost exclusively, since the Windows program is inexcusably bad. Theoretically any device with Bluetooth 4.0 should be able to talk to the Charge, but my Android tablet was unable to, so until I got my iPhone I was forced to use the Windows program along with a small USB FitBit dongle.

The Windows program has absolutely no other function then to sync with the Charge, Which in theory you can do anytime that the charge is within range. But my installation of Windows 7 ultimate was unable to perform this task without me specifically launching the program and telling it to sync.

With the exception of doing a little of the initial setup, other than that single function of retrieving information from the Charge, passing it on to the FitBit website and vice-versa, the Windows desktop program does nothing. Literally nothing.

The fact that the desktop app does nothing, forces you forces the users without a FitBit compatible phone or tablet to perform everything that ought to be able to be doable locally on the webpage.

Things like, choosing a watch face, or determining the order in which things are displayed, or determining what, if anything, a double tap on the watch face does.

Some other useful changes I would like to see are:

+ Personally, since the FitBit communicates via Bluetooth, I see no reason why the FitBit Bluetooth dongle that comes with the device can't be used by the computer that you plug it into as a Bluetooth dongle. They just need to write drivers specific to their dongle, which they already have, that have a way of seizing control of the dongle when it needs to transmit, and then return control of the dongle to the regular Bluetooth system when it's done. We've already paid for the Bluetooth dongle, we might as well be able to use it, even if we only ever use the app.

+ Most usefully, change the clock faces to show:
1) Remaining battery charge! (Could just be asterisks, periods, or even the pipe symbol | .)
2) The Day of the Week!
3) The Date! (MM/DD)
4) Option to display AM/PM with 12 hour watch faces.

+ Add the "Connected GPS" that the new Blaze boast's!

+ Of course, change the desktop program so that you can do all the things that you can do on both the website and the apps, on your computer.

+ Changing how the app displays your sleep data so that it includes the amount of time that you slept deeply, or were in interrupted sleep.

+ Making the website more intuitive.
+ Have the website display your sleep data in a useful manner.

+ A larger range of watch faces to choose from, not just the current four.
+ The option of an analog watch face.
+ Add a screen to the charge that displays at least some of your sleep data.
+ Allow the Charge to be accessed via Bluetooth, so that even phones unable to install the fit bit app can still send text and caller and information to it.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in))

text_fidelity_a:
Mountain House Just in Case 72 Hour Kit We do a lot of camping and living outdoors, and something we enjoy is easy to make food when we are outdoors. We look for ways to keep the cooler, extra stoves, skillets, dutch ovens and cast iron at home. I think we found our answer in Mountain House freeze dried entrees.

We purchased the Mountain House Just in Case 72 Hour Kit. In it we chose the Beef Stroganoff and took it to a scout meeting to try. During the scout meeting we talked about light weight backpacking as well as food options for emergency food at home.

After we boiled two cups of water we poured it into the pouch and zip locked it for 8 minutes. The contents where stirred and then served to many hungry scouts at the meeting. Every scout got a sample to try and a lot of them were hesitant. The overall surprise on their faces was priceless. They liked it and said it tasted great.

They wanted a pouch of the Beef Stroganoff for themselves. The scouts were surprised how easy the meal was to make and how simple the cleanup is. We did also like the zip lock feature not only for the re-hydrating process but also to keep the uneaten food for later if needed. They were also coming up with ways to reuse the pouch for other needs in the forest or on the trail to keep from throwing the empty pouch away.

Most of the scouts have never re-hydrated food or eaten MREs before. They were impressed with the ease of cooking and how lightweight it is to add to your day pack or back pack.

For camping, outings or emergency preparedness I would recommend Mountain House Just in Case 72 Hour Kit to have on hand. For one it has a long shelf life, for two you won’t starve as the contents of each pouch will satisfy a hungry kid or adult. A very tasty meal…especially in the middle of the forest!

Our only complaint (and the reason we deducted a star) is not all the water absorbed into the food, so it was very runny. The pack instructed to use 2 cups of water and I feel that was too much.
text_fidelity_b: Mountain House Just in Case 72 Hour Kit

text_fidelity_a:
Allen Sports Aluminum 2 Child Trailer/Single & Double Swivel Wheel Stroller This is an initial impressions commentary less than it is a review. I plan on following up once I've had at least a month's worth of activity with it. Here in Chicago, the weather has been varying at the time of this review, so we've been able to use this only about a solid week's worth.

The night I received it I assembled it immediately. I've put together a few strollers, so I didn't intend on taking longer than twenty minutes. Not with this stroller. It took me almost an hour. The instructions came in two parts: one sheet indicating that it may be difficult to unfold at first, and the main instructions. Indeed, the stroller is very difficult to unfold at first, and it is difficult to fold back.
The instructions were not very coherent; the illustrations, instead of being reference models as in most manuals, were black-and-white photographs which made it difficult to discern exactly what they were trying to portray. Half the time I was trying to figure it out, and ended up going with my gut-feeling (which, thankfully to my previous stroller assembly experiences, led me to the correct outcomes).

Unfolding it the first time proved very difficult. Again, I did this myself with the assumption that it wouldn't be very difficult, so I did have a harder than usual unfolding it into its locked position. Once everything was assembled (mind you, you will need to provide your own tools as mine came with the wrong sized hex/L wrench and was missing the other tool, whatever it was), I was ready to put it in the basement for the time being. We live in a pretty spacious apartment building with plenty of basement storage, and that's where we store all of our strollers, etc. Folding it back was pretty rough; I could not for the life of me tell where the unlocking mechanisms were due to the poorly lit photographs, so I had to figure it out. Once I got it, however, one side of the locks was very hard to unlock.

On our first walks, however, the stroll was fine. It glides pretty smoothly, but I wish the handlebar had an easier and quicker way to adjust the angle, as our previous strollers have. As I mentioned before, it's very difficult to unfold and requires two people, so when my wife tried to get the stroller out on her own she was unable to due to the force required. Who knows how this will be with time.

As I've mentioned, I will follow up with a more experienced review.
text_fidelity_b: Allen Sports Aluminum 2 Child Trailer/Single & Double Swivel Wheel Stroller

text_fidelity_a:
JOROTO X2 Stationary Exercise Bike | X2PRO Bluetooth Magnetic Belt Drive Indoor Cycling Bike, 300 Pounds Loads Fitness Cycle Bikes The UPS deliveryman carried this box to the front door with ease, but I quickly learned that a 108 lb., smooth, cardboard box is NOT that easy to maneuver. So just be aware this is a heavy shipment!

I was worried this was going to be a cheap and flimsy bike, but that's not the case in any way! This thing is welded, heavy gauge steel with a thick paint job (probably not powder coated). The handles are equally solid with a thick rubber grip, probably hot dipped. Basically, no amount of sweaty hands are going to cause the grip to deteriorate. The mechanics are practically silent.

Assembly is a cinch. There are 4 bolts used to attach the feet, three adjustable handles to attach the seat and handle, and two pedals to screw on. All of the required tools are in the box.

I've only ridden on it once, but the seat is soft (not that it matters if you're standing). The electronic display is of utmost cheapness, though. I was afraid that I was going to break it when installing the (included) AA batteries. It provides very basic information such as time, distance, "speed", and "calories" but there is no input for height and weight.

I'm waiting on a cadence sensor that will attach to one of the crank arms, and plan to use that with an app to get better feedback on pace. I also downloaded the Peloton app (30 day free trial) and was able to follow along just fine with the beginners ride. The resistance knob doesn't have a numeric scale (just +/-) so you'll have to judge for yourself based on how it feels.

Final thought is regarding the maneuverability. The front wheels are a bit small and made of a hard plastic so it will be hard to roll across carpet. You can tell from the photo we have a hard floor, and if it gets caught on debris, it may easily get stuck or scratch the floor.

Overall, I'm impressed with the build quality, assembly and performance. Only negatives are the ultra cheap display, lack of any integrated wireless technology (BYO), and the small wheels to move it around.
text_fidelity_b: JOROTO X2 Stationary Exercise Bike | X2PRO Bluetooth Magnetic Belt Drive Indoor Cycling Bike, 300 Pounds Loads Fitness Cycle Bikes

text_fidelity_a: ONGUARD Bulldog Mini U-Lock (Black, 3.55 x 5.52-Inch) If you've avoided U-locks in the past because they were so big and heavy, give this one a try. The "mini" size should work on any good quality bike rack, though it is not big enough for parking meters. It is also not big enough to lock both wheels; use another lock or a cable to secure the other wheel. Because of the smaller size, the lock is a reasonable weight and size. The package comes with a generous set of 5 keys, for people who are always losing theirs (leave a spare at work and at your friends house and in your car). Some people are complaining about the lock jamming after years of use in the rain, but realistically all locks will have that problem; you really need to oil any lock after every use in the rain. For the $20 price, I really couldn't ask for any more. There are more secure locks out there, but for much higher prices and heavier weights.

text_fidelity_a:
Swagman XC2 Hitch Mount Bike Rack , Black, 2-Inch Receiver Easy to setup and adjust, feels sturdy and secure. It really would take a bit of effort to remove a bike from it if you have it locked down.

Seems like a really good value.

There were a few stumbling blocks I encountered, though. First, the locking hitch pin that Sawgman sells is a bit expensive, compared to other locking pins you can find. However, because the rack had a threaded hole, a standard 1/2” pin won’t fit through. I ended up just yawing the supplied pin, and used a small Master Lock with a small enough shackle diameter to fit. Probably not as secure as the proprietary locking pin, but it should be enough to dissuade anyone looking for a quick grab and go.

Speaking of shackle diameter, it was a bit of a challenge to find the perfect locks to use on the bars. Your typical MasterLock is about 7mm, which is too big; and 5mm was small enough that you could still pull the trigger and move the bar up with ease. In the end I found the MasterLock 141T set of two locks (Keyed alike) with a 6mm shackle was the best fit. The shackle is just small enough to fit through the hole, but thick enough to keep the trigger secure.

So the TLDR, but a lock with a 6mm diameter shackle to secure your bikes.
text_fidelity_b: Swagman XC2 Hitch Mount Bike Rack , Black, 2-Inch Receiver

text_fidelity_a:
Thule Rodvault Fly Fishing Rod Carrier This thing is totally awesome. I was actually unaware that such fishing rod carriers existed. And of course, I barely had to browse other models to tell Thule would be a top contender.

Construction is fantastic. Rigid metal tubes and hardened plastic casing make "vault" an acceptable term for this.

One thing I didn't realize was that with this one (unlike the tackle fishing carriers), the length is not adjustable. The tubing is the same diameter for the entire length, so the two 5' sections connect in the middle with a compression connector tightened by hex screws. Because of this, you probably need to lock both parts of this to your rooftop rack, which leads to me locking...

...Locking this up is probably the weak point for me. This is unfortunate, because I always want better locking on any device, but this one isn't even as good as I might expect out of Thule. For one thing, it doesn't have the "one key" feature that Thule started using at some point (but you had to special order your device with your key type already if you wanted to go with that, so maybe consumers were too lazy to do it and the company gave up on it...not sure). Worse, though - and a real concern - is that this and my tackle vault use the same key, which leads me to wonder if I am able to open up and steal from any Thule rodvault I see out there in the wild? (Of course, I'd like to believe that anyone with enough money to buy a rodvault would be unlikely to steal fishing stuff from another person, but who knows...). Also, you need padlocks to lock the vault to the rack, which isn't that big of a deal, but I've seen other equipment with integrated locks that used the same key as the rest of the equipment, so it could be better.

This is big and heavy. More so than I expected. That adds some sense of value to it, but it also has me rethinking my storage place, especially considering its 10' permanent length unless I want to disassemble it with every use.

I'm also curious if this would hold some deep sea poles. I think so, but don't have any yet to try for myself.

In conclusion, it's hard to not be impressed with this thing, and yet I see some areas for improvement, mostly in the locking scheme. It is hard not to give this a full five stars simply because of its excellent sturdiness and bringing a whole new excellent way to transport large, expensive poles with even a small car, and without having to worry about them at all, for the most part.
text_fidelity_b: Thule Rodvault Fly Fishing Rod Carrier

text_fidelity_a:
Covermates Bicycle Cover - Light Weight Polyester, Mesh Vent, Elastic Hem, Power Sports Covers-Khaki After going through 2 of those cheap plastic covers over the past few years I decided it was time to invest in a "real" cover for my bicycle which spends it's entire time outside my little apartment or where I work.

After measuring the bicycle (70L x 48H x 24W) and looking around on-line for several days, I got it narrowed down to this one from The Cover Store, and the one from Empire covers.

I went with this one because it had a fastener on the bottom to hold the cover in place (optional on the Empire cover), and I liked the tan color better than the black Empire cover.

I'm very pleased with the quality of this cover. I have my handlebars and seat set quite high, and often leave a small handlebar bag in place, and this cover still fits perfectly, covering the wheels all the way to the ground.

I'm not sure what the other folks that complained of a generic style cover got, but the one I received was obviously tailored specifically for a bicycle, and with the elastic hem fits like a glove.

I can't speak for it's durability or water resistance as I just got it, but a brief splash of water just ran off, and it seems to be made of very durable material.

I will say though, that I was so impressed that I just ordered another one.

Edit-Sept 28, 2011: I've had both covers for nearly a month now, and I'm VERY happy so far. I use my bike to commute to work, so I have a cover at both ends. Because of the elastic around the bottom, it took me a few times to figure out how to quickly and easily get the cover on and off, but here is what I've found works well for me:

First, after getting the cover on and positioned the way I wanted it, I used a magic marker to draw a fairly large triangle over the seat with the tip pointing forward and an arrow inside the triangle, also pointing forward.

Then I put a big L with a circle around it over the left handgrip and a big R with a circle around it over the right hand grip.

These 3 markers help me quickly orient and position the cover when getting ready to put it on.

What's important to realize is that the elastic around the bottom has a natural tendency to catch on things, so you simply have to learn what those things are on your particular bike and work around them.

I start by finding the triangle marker and placing that over the seat, then I get the elastic over the handlebars and down over the front wheel. Then I get the rear of the cover down over the rear wheel and around both foot pedals and the dérailleur. It takes about 2 minutes.

To get the cover off I just reverse the procedure, getting the elastic over the foot pedals and the dérailleur and then off the back wheel, then off the seat and finally over the handle bars. It takes about a minute.

This cover has plenty of room, but it's tailored in such a way as to fit nicely, and with the elastic around the bottom it's very secure. I'll report back after we get a few rains, but so far these covers are winners.

Edit (August 25, 2012): Well, I've had my two covers for a year of daily commuting to and from work, and I'm happy to report that they've met all my expectations for durability and water resistance. They still look almost new and I've had no problems with the seams leaking or showing any wear. Definitely a good investment.

Edit (September 5, 2013): Ok, it's been another year. I still use both covers for my daily commute to and from work, and they both still look really good. Only minor blemishes from being used outside all the time, but seriously, they still look very nice. Seams still all good, no wear. Elastic still like new. I've used the buckle several times during very windy weather, but probably didn't need to, because the elastic does such a good job. Yes, it still takes some time get them on and off, but I don't mind, and it's worth it to me for the excellent fit they provide. See you next year : )

Edit (January 16, 2015): Another year and a half. I really do love these covers. It's funny, people are always commenting on my "new" bicycle, and they can't believe it when I tell them it's over 15 years old. Yes, I clean and lube everything twice a year, but this bike lives outside, and it's these covers that help keep it in such good shape. A very worth while investment, and yes, the covers, although with a few stains here and there, still look practically new and function perfectly.
text_fidelity_b: Covermates Bicycle Cover - Light Weight Polyester, Mesh Vent, Elastic Hem, Power Sports Covers-Khaki

text_fidelity_a:
Ferexer 48 oz Sports Borosilicate Glass Water Bottle with Bamboo Lid with Neoprene Sleeve CONTEXT:
After watching a documentary about teflon and plastic etcetera, and learning that all similar products leech into the water, I opted to start using glass. After using a Hydro, I was a little bit bummed that my water wouldn't be cold AF for hours on end, but I figured it was worth the sacrifice. I have smaller glass bottles, but with as much as I workout, I needed a way to track and increase my intake. I found this one and immediately needed it because of its size!

PROS:
- The neoprene sleeve it comes with actually does a pretty good job of keeping the water cold AND helps with keeping the condensation at bay. It never gets soaking wet.
- It holds so much water! One bottle of this a day is one 1.4 liters.
- Water just tastes so much better. I don't care what anyone says... water tastes better out of glass.
- The handle addition on the neoprene is a huge plus! It helps with lugging this thing around.

CONS:
- This isn't really a con for me, BUT I know it will be for others. The water doesn't stay cold for hours... I live in Hawaiʻi, so naturally, it gets warm pretty quick (but keep reading for tips). If you live somewhere cold, like Washington, I don't think you'll really have a problem. :)
- Obviously, this bottle is pretty freakin large. So carrying it around can be a b-word.

TIPS:
- I learned that putting ice in my bottle helps a lot with keeping it cold throughout the day (not even kidding). I usually fill the bottle with 1/4 ice and the rest with filtered water. By the time I am getting to the bottom of my bottle, the ice has melted, but the water is still cold.

OVERALL:
I can't recommend this bottle enough. It is perfect for me!
text_fidelity_b: Ferexer 48 oz Sports Borosilicate Glass Water Bottle with Bamboo Lid with Neoprene Sleeve

text_fidelity_a:
RedSwing Small Folding Table Portable 2 Feet, Small Foldable Table Adjustable Height, Lightweight Aluminum Camping Table, 15.7 in x 23.6 in x 19 in I bought the 24x24 table to use as a small laptop desk to work remotely from my camper. Overall I'm happy with it for the price, but have to give it 4 stars due to some small issues mentioned below.

Pros:
Cheap
Seems durable
Takes almost no room when folded up
Easy to assemble and disassemble
Looks pretty nice

Cons:
Pretty wobbly - because it's basically thin aluminum, despite reinforcements on the legs the table moves around quite a bit. If you pin it against the wall and make sure the legs are really spread out it's workable, but still wobbly.
Sharp edges - there are some sharp edges that can really cut/bite you as your folding and unfolding the table. About 30 seconds with a file could fix this problem so it's a bummer they didn't bother.
Uneven top - the top has a crease where the table folds in half. This makes the top uneven, so if you have a laptop in the middle of it it kind of teeter-totters, which is a bit annoying.
